He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State Spartans]], earning [[Big Ten Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big Ten Player of the Year]] honors and leading the team to a national title in 2000. == College career == [[File:Michigan state bask 42 peterson.jpg|thumb|left|120px|Peterson's #42 was retired by Michigan State University in 2009]] Born in [[Flint, Michigan]], Peterson played for the Michigan State and helped lead them to the 2000 [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA title]]. In his senior year at MSU, Peterson led the team in scoring, field goal percentage, and [[free throw]] percentage. He had a team-high 30 double-digit scoring efforts. He was voted [[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] Player of the Year and First Team All-Big Ten, and he placed as first or second team All-American on five different polls. He was selected 21st overall by the [[Toronto Raptors|Raptors]] in the [[2000 NBA draft]], and was a starter in the majority of their games during his first three seasons. On January 17, 2009, MSU retired his number 42 with MSU's other all-time greats before their game against the [[Illinois Fighting Illini]]. == NBA career == === Toronto Raptors === Drafted in the first round by the Raptors in 2000, Peterson was a fan favorite from the moment he stepped on the floor. While enjoying some early success in his professional career, Peterson's production faced a steady decline, before stepping up in the wake of the new era of Raptor youngsters being ushered in, taking on a more expansive leadership role and transforming himself into an elite perimeter defender, a clutch performer and consistent scorer. He is known for his three-point shooting, acrobatic shots, defense, and fearless driving to the basket. On December 28, 2005, Peterson set a record for career games played as a Raptor, surpassing [[Alvin Williams]] with 418 games played. Peterson also leads the NBA in longest consecutive games played, appearing in 371 straight until November 22, 2006, when he missed his first game in over four years. Peterson posted career highs in points and rebounds averaging 16.8 points and 4.6 rebounds and threw in 2.3 assists per game through 82 games played in the [[2005–06 NBA season|2005–06 season]]. Perhaps the biggest highlight of his career occurred against the [[Washington Wizards]] on March 30, 2007, in a game that helped determine the two teams' playoff seeding. The Raptors trailed 109–106 with only 3.8 seconds left and no timeouts remaining. The Wizards' [[Michael Ruffin]] intercepted the full-court pass and tried to toss the ball high into the air so that the clock would run out. But the ball slipped from his hands and was not thrown high enough. There was still enough time on the clock as Peterson caught the ball and launched a "Hail Mary" three-pointer and sank it to send the game into overtime. Peterson only played 55 seconds in the game, with his first shift beginning with only 9.3 seconds left in the fourth quarter.[https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/pbp/200703300WAS.html Toronto Raptors at Washington Wizards Play-By-Play, March 30, 2007] The Raptors went on to defeat the Wizards, 123–118.[https://web.archive.org/web/20110111180358/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=270330027 Peterson's heave, Bosh's 37 spur Raptors past Wiz] After signing Bryan Colangelo, it became apparent that the re-building process of the Raptors would not include Peterson. It was only a matter of time before his contract expired in the summer of 2007 that he would be gone. === New Orleans Hornets === On July 13, 2007, the [[New Orleans Hornets]] signed Peterson to a four-year contract, worth $23 million.{{cite web| url = https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2935681| title = Sources: Peterson agrees to $23M deal with Hornets| date = July 13, 2007}} === Oklahoma City Thunder === On July 8, 2010, the Hornets traded Peterson along with #11 overall pick in the 2010 draft, [[Cole Aldrich]], to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] for two 2010 first-round draft picks (#21, [[Craig Brackins]] and #26, [[Quincy Pondexter]]).[http://www.nba.com/2010/news/06/24/hornets.thunder.trade/index.html Hornets to trade No. 11 pick Aldrich to Thunder] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100628033442/http://www.nba.com/2010/news/06/24/hornets.thunder.trade/index.html |date=June 28, 2010 }} === Charlotte Bobcats === On February 24, 2011, Peterson was traded to the [[Charlotte Bobcats]] along with [[D.J. White]] in exchange for [[Nazr Mohammed]].{{cite web | url = http://www.nba.com/bobcats/release_peterson_white_110224.html | title = Bobcats Acquire Morris Peterson and D.J. White from Thunder | work = NBA.com | date = February 24, 2011 | access-date = February 25, 2011}} He was waived four days later when his contract was bought out by the Bobcats.{{cite web | url = http://www.nba.com/bobcats/release_peterson_waived_110228.html | title = Bobcats Waive Morris Peterson | work = NBA.com | date = February 28, 2011 | access-date = February 28, 2011}} Peterson's final NBA game was played on December 12, 2010, in a 106 - 77 win over the Cleveland Cavaliers where he recorded 2 points. == Broadcasting career == On January 14, 2015, [[The Sports Network|TSN]] announced that Peterson would join their broadcast team as an analyst. For the network's package of [[Toronto Raptors]] games, Peterson joined TSN's broadcast team of [[Jack Armstrong (sportscaster)|Jack Armstrong]], [[Leo Rautins]], [[Matt Devlin (sportscaster)|Matt Devlin]], and [[Rod Black]] both in the [[The Sports Network|TSN]] Studio and on-site at the [[Air Canada Centre]] in [[Toronto]], Ontario. Peterson will also deliver analysis for [[SportsCentre]] and appear throughout the network's expanded NCAA coverage, including TSN's wall-to-wall coverage of [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA March Madness]]. As of 2017, Peterson is no longer an analyst on TSN.{{cite web | url = https://www.tsn.ca/morris-mo-pete-peterson-joins-tsn-s-broadcast-team-1.182503 | title = Morris 'Mo Pete' Peterson joins TSN's broadcast team | work = TSN.ca | date = January 14, 2014 | access-date = January 14, 2014}} == Restaurant == On January 23, 2018, Peterson, in a partnership with Viktor Palushaj, opened "MoPetes Sports Retreat" just outside his hometown of Flint in neighboring [[Flint Township, Michigan]]. The menu features Michigan inspired dishes such as The Flintstones Combos, Flint-Town Reuben sandwich, the Izzo sub, and The National Champ Philly cheesesteak sandwich.{{cite web | url = https://www.mlive.com/news/flint/index.ssf/2018/01/morris_peterson_sports_bar_now.html | title = Morris Peterson sports bar now open in Flint Township| date = January 24, 2018}} == Accolades == *
